Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{6}^{-3}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-\frac{113}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-3}^{6}(9f(x)+8x)\,\text{d}x & =9{\int }_{-3}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,8{\int }_{-3}^{6}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =9(-\frac{113}{9})\,+\,8\cdot \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{-3}^{6} \\  & =-113\,+\,8\cdot \frac{{6}^{2}-(-3)^{2}}{2} \\  & =-113\,+\,8\cdot \frac{27}{2} \\  & =-113\,+\,108 \\  & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$
